about.title: Willows Slip & Fall & Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Slip and fall accidents happen fast — a wet floor at a market on Sycamore Street, a cracked walkway near W Wood Street, or poor lighting in a parking lot off Rt 162. In Willows, these incidents often occur at grocery stores, gas stations, and small businesses that serve the community. California law requires proving the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and failed to address it in time. That's why documentation matters so much: photos of the hazard, witness names, and surveillance footage can make or break a claim, especially before video gets overwritten. If you were hurt on someone else's property in Willows, contact us for a free review of your case. Our team will explain your options with no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a Willows Premises Liability Claim

items.title: Proving Notice
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and didn't fix or warn about it in reasonable time. We can help gather evidence — like maintenance logs or prior complaints — to establish that notice.

items.title: Preserving Surveillance Footage
items.desc: Many Willows businesses record over surveillance video within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of footage can be critical to showing what actually happened.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by your share of blame but isn't eliminated just because you were partly at fault. Our team can help address how fault gets allocated in your case.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Willows?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a city building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early formal claim. It's best to have your situation reviewed as soon as possible so you don't miss a critical date.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for my own fall?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover compensation even if you were partly at fault, though your recovery may be reduced by your percentage of responsibility. This is decided case by case based on the specific facts. Our team can walk you through how this might apply to your situation.

items.question: Will you handle my Willows case directly?
items.answer: Yes. We handle premises liability cases directly. Once you contact us, our team reviews your case and typically works on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless we recover compensation for you.
